newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Bright future seen for ISS.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Bright future seen for ISS.

text.p: Analysts on Tuesday shrugged off Danish cleaning group ISS' heavy 1996 net loss and focused instead on underlying figures and future prospects in the wake of the sale U.S. unit ISS Inc, whose false accounting allowed losses to build up unseen.
"It looks reasonable, particularly without ISS Inc. Operating results in the Scandinavian and European divisions actually look a little better than expected," an analyst said.
"Given generally stable conditions (the share) will outperform from now on. I believe that many people will come to see ISS with new eyes," he added.

The group earlier reported a 1.86 billion crown net loss for 1996, compared to a revised 20 million crown profit the year before but said that with last December's sale of ISS Inc ending its liablities it looked foward to improved profitablity and a more stable share price in 1997.
The market apparently agreed and despite the bottom-line loss the group's share had traded up to 181 crowns by mid-morning, from Monday's closing 178.2.
Group turnover was up by a billion crowns, to 15.396 from 1995's 14,391, and operating profit rose to 619 million crowns in 1996 from 572 million the year before.
Analysts' average forecasts were for turnover of 15.750 billion crowns, with operating profit of 630 million.
